subject: born-again minimalists
one_liner: The home-improvement warehouse for people buying everything they need to own less.
brand_voice_notes: Bare treats becoming a minimalist as a substantial home-improvement project. Use the calm, practical voice of a store associate helping someone make an increasingly expensive mistake. Name the goods, quantities and consequences. Let the customer remain proud of the purchase. Apply the frozen anti-ai-slop skill throughout: no em dashes, corporate enthusiasm, throat-clearing or explanatory endings. Compared with the recent digest, this premise centers on renovation, repeated tool rental and decorating indecision. Prices are physical project bundles rather than memberships; testimonials describe what happened at home after checkout.
demo_screen_concept: One project-shopping screen opens on 'Clear the kitchen counter' with the goal 'Six mugs out of sight.' A retail header contains search, department navigation and a selected pickup store. Below it, product cards show a wall cabinet for $129, mounting hardware for $21 and an installation assessment for $39, already selected in a project cart totaling $189. Each card has a product photograph, price, availability and a plain Add or Remove control. Two further products are a four-hour drill rental for $19 and twelve white paint samples for $48. Adding either updates the cart and total immediately. The cart keeps the original six-mug goal visible above its growing purchase list. Selecting the drill reveals its return time; selecting paint reveals twelve nearly identical swatches. Pickup and delivery controls update fulfillment details without leaving the screen. A reset restores the original project. The screen retains the recognizable warehouse-shopping sequence of project list, stock check, product selection and fulfillment.

hero.h1: Your clear-out needs a delivery truck.
hero.sub: Bare supplies new minimalists with cabinets, rented tools and twelve shades of white. Clearing six mugs off the counter now requires an installation appointment.

features.title: Clear the counter.
features.blurb: Tell the project calculator you want six mugs out of sight. It adds a wall cabinet, mounting hardware and an installation visit. You now need your landlord's permission to tidy up.

features.title: Rent back the drill.
features.blurb: You gave away your drill because you hardly used it. Reserve the same model for four hours whenever another job comes up. By the fifth rental, you've spent more than it cost to remain someone who doesn't own a drill.

features.title: Choose one white.
features.blurb: Order twelve paint samples for a calm, blank wall. Paint a square of each and compare them throughout the day. Guests keep asking who did the mural.

observations.behavior: People newly committed to minimalism often want possessions hidden rather than gone, and treat a clear surface as proof of progress.
observations.mechanic: A home-improvement project calculator converts a small household goal into a cabinet, mounting hardware and an installation assessment.
observations.consequence: Putting away six mugs becomes a building alteration requiring a landlord's permission. After installation, the step stool needed to reach them occupies the cleared counter.

observations.behavior: People purge useful equipment to reduce their possession count, then defend the decision when they need the equipment again.
observations.mechanic: Timed tool rental lets the customer repeatedly reserve the same drill without owning it.
observations.consequence: Five rentals cost more than the donated drill. The customer preserves their minimalist identity while their spouse keeps the evidence in the newly empty drawer.

observations.behavior: People seeking a calm home can become so invested in choosing the perfect neutral that the decision takes over the room.
observations.mechanic: Paint comparison encourages ordering sample pots, applying test squares and checking their appearance in different light.
observations.consequence: The blank wall becomes a twelve-square mural. Admiration from visitors persuades the minimalist to buy a large frame for the unfinished decision.

source_product_patterns: Warehouse departments and searchable product listings organized around home-improvement tasks.
Project calculators that turn a stated goal into a materials list.
Add-all project carts with individual quantities, prices and a running total.
Local-store availability, aisle locations and scheduled pickup.
Delivery selection for bulky cabinets and larger project orders.
Tool rental with a stated hire period and return time.
Paint samples and side-by-side color comparison.
Installation assessments followed by a separate installation quote.
editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: Plan a clear-out, opening the project cart. Recognizable product visual: a warehouse shopping interface with cabinet, hardware and service listings beside a running order summary. Opening hierarchy: compact Bare identity and studio credit, large headline, concise explanation, CTA, then a full-width working product preview. Give the preview enough space to show the six-mug goal and $189 cart together. On mobile, retain that order and place the cart directly after its products. Follow with three distinct feature passages, customer accounts and a joined comparison of Counter, Room and House project bundles. Proposed artwork one is a documentary kitchen photograph showing six mugs beneath a taped cabinet outline while an installer measures the wall; it explains the scale of work generated by a tiny clear-out. Proposed artwork two shows twelve nearly identical paint-test squares on an otherwise bare wall, photographed like a proudly displayed artwork; it explains how indecision becomes decoration. Catalogue cutouts of the cabinet, drill and sample pots serve as selectable product evidence in the preview and demo. Keep goals, prices, quantities, swatch names and captions in live text. The retail workflow supplies the structure; the customer's carefully purchased simplicity supplies the visual identity.

references.reference: MUJI storage-box packaging and storage-department displays
references.cues: Translucent containers, plain paper bands, small factual labels, repeated dimensions and tightly aligned shelving.
references.application: Use measured product cutouts, narrow specification lines and orderly shelf-like rows. Set headings in Archivo Narrow and body text and controls in IBM Plex Sans. Let the expanding cart interrupt an otherwise controlled presentation. Create original identity and packaging without reproducing MUJI marks.

references.cues: White metal, pale timber, uncluttered counters and everyday kitchen objects photographed against deliberate empty space.
references.application: Use bright domestic photography, pale birch details and graphite outlines. Show the same six ordinary mugs consistently so the audience can judge how much infrastructure has been bought to conceal them. Borrow the material restraint without copying products, trademarks or compositions.

audience_design.landing_application: Choose the visual world of a newly reorganized kitchen rather than a generic luxury minimalist home. Use chalk white #FAFBF8, putty #E4E6DF, graphite #2D342F and muted bottle green #4E6255, with restrained rust #A54532 for price annotations and return-time warnings. Archivo Narrow gives headings the character of storage packaging; IBM Plex Sans keeps explanations and controls readable, with tabular numerals for prices. Photography is bright, frontal and matter-of-fact. Broad shelf-like sections and aligned specification rows organize the page, while two large domestic photographs reveal the consequences. Empty space establishes the customer's aspiration; visible goods and purchase totals explain what it costs.
audience_design.demo_application: Carry the same white, putty, graphite and bottle-green system into a denser shopping workspace. Preserve department navigation, search, product cards, stock information, a persistent cart and pickup or delivery selection. Product photographs sit on consistent white grounds; dimensions and prices align like shelf labels. Use simple borders and clear selected states rather than decorative containers. On narrow screens, stack product listings and the cart in reading order while keeping a compact cart-total control available. The audience identity appears in materials, typography and obsessively orderly presentation; the source service remains recognizable through shopping, rental and fulfillment actions.

design_direction.style: Measured storage-catalog minimalism: narrow packaging typography, shelf-like horizontal groupings, bright product cutouts and quiet cabinet joinery.

fonts.pairing: Host-approved Archivo Narrow + IBM Plex Sans; IBM Plex functional typography from the bundled Financial Trust pairing, Archivo packaging display per approved audience brief.

design_direction.archetype: Product demo + features, adapted to a measured home-storage catalogue: full-width project-shopping preview after the proposition; shelf-like feature stories, customer accounts and joined project comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 150ms button color changes; immediate cart calculations; no ambient animation; reduced-motion removes transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Broad left-aligned headline alongside concise copy and action, followed immediately by a live cabinet/hardware/service shopping preview and six-mug goal with $189 total. Product preview precedes campaign artworks.
design_direction.design_review: Compared all seven host digest entries: no matching style/palette/fonts tuple. Cabinet joinery, exact catalog proportions and nearly-white paint patches differ from salvage tags, fan sleeves, pond contours, workout chapters, huddle contours, seed cells and parcel tabs. Approved audience palette and fonts override generic library selections.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: Bare borrows the calm of storage packaging and white-metal kitchen organizers. An open-cupboard identity and measured shelf rows make the expanding shopping list feel perfectly reasonable. Original cupboard geometry and narrow wordmark differ from recent salvage frames and character marks.

Direction A: a bespoke confident lowercase/initial-cap narrow sans wordmark beside an original open-cupboard symbol: hinged door swung outward, visibly empty interior, bold spare silhouette. Refined storage packaging and white-metal kitchen-organizer visual world. Dark bottle green #4E6255 and graphite #2D342F, solid chalk #FAFBF8 background. Practical, quiet, memorable at 24px.
